original_title: Trump Fires DOJ Prosecutor to Pursue Retaliatory Case Against Comey

existing.title: Trump Fires DOJ Prosecutor to Pursue Retaliatory Case Against Comey
existing.description_short: Trump Fires DOJ Prosecutor to Pursue Retaliatory Case Against Comey
existing.description_long: In September 2025, Trump orchestrated the removal of U.S. Attorney Erik Siebert from the Eastern District of Virginia after Siebert, following a five-month investigation, concluded there was not sufficient evidence to charge former FBI Director James Comey. Trump publicly pressured Siebert to resign in an Oval Office address, then fired him when he refused to quit. Trump appointed Lindsey Halligan — a former personal attorney with no prosecutorial experience — as his replacement. Halligan was sworn in on September 22, 2025, and three days later secured a federal grand jury indictment against Comey on charges of making a false statement to Congress and obstructing a congressional proceeding related to 2020 testimony — just before the five-year statute of limitations expired on September 30. Halligan accomplished the indictment despite the full grand jury never reviewing the final indictment text; only the foreperson and one other juror saw it. Federal judges described the investigation as showing a disturbing pattern of profound investigative missteps and potential prosecutorial misconduct. On November 24, 2025, Judge Cameron Currie dismissed the indictment, ruling Halligan had been unlawfully appointed. The DOJ appealed. Comey had famously been fired by Trump during his first term while overseeing the Russia investigation.
